payload.title: Reading TCP_INFO Safely
payload.summary: Capture a narrow course-owned TCP snapshot from Linux TCP_INFO, copy only fields covered by the returned option length, and map observations into the course state model.

prerequisites: Review Lesson 7's state model and the stream-socket lesson
Know the roles of MSS, unacknowledged segments, loss, retransmission, RTT, RTT variation, and congestion-control state
Use Linux headers and a Linux kernel implementing TCP_INFO
No elevated capabilities, packet capture, external network access, fixed port, or timing tool
outcomes: Treat returned socklen_t as the boundary for every copied field
Use presence bits so zero is not confused with absence
Check stable invariants without depending on volatile performance values

payload.title: Each field is copied only when returned socklen_t covers the complete Linux struct tcp_info member; the matching presence bit distinguishes an observed zero from an absent field.

fields.name: snd_mss
fields.meaning: tcpi_snd_mss: current send maximum segment size

fields.name: rcv_mss
fields.meaning: tcpi_rcv_mss: current receive maximum segment size

fields.name: rtt_us
fields.meaning: tcpi_rtt: smoothed round-trip-time estimate in microseconds

fields.name: rttvar_us
fields.meaning: tcpi_rttvar: round-trip-time variation estimate in microseconds

invariants: State must be present and map to a known course state.
A present send MSS must be nonzero.
A present receive MSS must be nonzero.
A present RTT estimate must be nonzero.
Observed loss requires a present, nonzero current or lifetime retransmission count.
The presence mask must not contain unknown bits.
Absent optional tail fields are valid and retain zero values with clear presence bits.

payload.exercise: Implement exercise.c by zeroing struct tcp_info, initializing socklen_t to the full structure size, checking every field by offset and size, rejecting unsupported sockets cleanly, and avoiding retained pointers, allocation, or global state.
payload.reference: Compare against the linux-reference preset, which copies into the public course snapshot and maps Linux states to the Lesson 7 vocabulary.
checks: Loopback client and server endpoints map to established with required fields present
MSS and RTT observations are present and nonzero when covered by the returned structure
Listener state mapping, unknown state handling, and Unix socketpair rejection are deterministic
Synthetic snapshots report documented violation bits without turning invariant failures into system errors

allowed: Loopback IPv4 sockets bound to port zero
A narrow course-owned representation independent of struct tcp_info
excluded: Using snapshots as synchronization, congestion-control interfaces, or predictions of the next packet
Parsing /proc, invoking ss, exposing unstable new kernel fields, or benchmarking loopback
Exact RTT, RTT variance, congestion window, queue counter, or endpoint-equality assertions
